International Admissions
Applicants with an academic history outside of the USA might be required to fulfill additional requirements in order to be considered for admission to a graduate program at the School of Engineering & Applied Science. Please click on the following options below to learn more about these requirements.
English Language Exam Requirements
English Language Exam Requirements
Applicants who have not completed a post-secondary degree from a US institution are required to submit TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or PTE Academic scores to GW Engineering to be considered for admission.
Scores may not be more than two years old.
TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo all administer at-home testing options.
Minimum Score Requirements
The following are the minimum scores required to be considered for admission to the School of Engineering & Applied Science. Depending on individual scores, students may be required to enroll in English for Academic Purposes during their first semester (see the English for Academic Purposes (EAP) Policy below).
IELTS*
6.0 overall
TOEFL*
4.0 overall for exams taken after January 21, 2026
81 for exams taken before January 21, 2026
Duolingo English Test
115 score or higher on the Duolingo English Test.
PTE Academic
58 overall
*Please note that we do not accept TOEFL MyBest or IELTS One Skill Retake scores.
Exceptions
Exceptions are granted to applicants who meet either of the following criteria:
Hold (or will earn before matriculation) a bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degree from a regionally accredited institution located in the United States or an institution in a country on the list of exempted countries.
Hold (or will earn before matriculation) a combined bachelor’s degree where a minimum of 2 years were completed at an institution located in the United States or in a country on the list of exempted countries.
If you are unsure whether you qualify for an exception, please contact us at [email protected].
English for Academic Purposes (EAP) Policy
International students who have a TOEFL score below 100 (for exams taken prior to January 21, 2026) or below 5.0 overall (for exams taken after January 21, 2026), an IELTS score below a 7.0, or a Duolingo English Test score below 130 are required to satisfactorily complete an English for Academic Purposes (EAP) course in the first semester. Your admission letter will indicate which EAP course you are required to take.
EAP 6110: Academic Writing and Research I (3 credits)
EAP 6111: Academic Writing and Research II (3 credits)
You will take a short exam in the first class of the semester to ensure you are enrolled in the correct EAP course. You may need to change EAP courses if the results of your exam indicate another course is better suited for you.
EAP course credits do not count towards your degree credit requirements or your degree GPA. If you do not successfully complete the EAP course, you may be required to take the course again, you may be put on academic probation, or you may be terminated from your degree program.
For additional information on the content of each course, please visit the EAP website.
Students who are assigned an EAP condition and wish to submit new scores to attempt to waive the requirement must submit them prior to July 1 if starting in a Fall semester or November 1 if starting in a Spring semester.
Sending Test Scores to GW
For IELTS: GW accepts electronic or paper Test Report Forms directly from IELTS. Please follow instructions on the IELTS website to submit your scores electronically or by mail to us at the address below. Alternatively, you can email us at [email protected] with a PDF of your score report including the TRF number.
For TOEFL: Please follow the instructions outlined by ETS. Use institution code 5246 when sending scores to GW. Alternatively, you can email us at [email protected] with a PDF of your score report including your appointment number.
For PTE Academic: Please follow the instructions outlined by Pearson to send scores reports to GW. No institution code is required. Alternatively, you can email us at [email protected] with a PDF of your score report including your score report code.
For Duolingo English Test: Please follow the instructions outlined by Duolingo. Select "The George Washington University School of Engineering and Applied Science" when sending scores to GW.
If you elect to send any of your test score reports by mail, please send them to the address below and our team will verify the scores with the corresponding test administration:
School of Engineering & Applied Science
Office of Graduate Admissions & Student Services
800 22nd St. NW, Suite 2900
Washington, DC 20052
Submitting Foreign Transcripts
All transcripts must be scanned and attached to the online application form. Please do not mail hard copies of transcripts during the application process.
Applicants who attended and/or received a degree from a foreign institution must submit transcripts in English as well as the original language.
Applicants who attended an institution in which English was the primary language of instruction, but not situated in an English-speaking country, must also submit transcripts in both English and the original language.
For transcripts from institutions in India: please scan individual marksheets demonstrating the grade received in each course for each semester, including any and all backlogs from the degree-granting or autonomous institution.
GW Engineering does not accept transcript evaluations by third-party organizations (ex. WES) in place of the original transcripts from the issuing institution.
Visa Request Documents
It is not mandatory to submit the visa request form or other visa-related documents as part of the application package.
Although there is a section on the application where you can upload these documents, it is not necessary to do so. You will only be required to provide these documents once you have received admission to GW Engineering and accepted your admissions offer. Providing or not providing these documents does not penalize or delay your application's review in any way.
